fields.name: enrollmentType
fields.doc: Enrollment type detected by the agent: "v1" (Autopilot Classic/ESP) or "v2" (Windows Device Preparation)

fields.name: isHybridJoin
fields.doc: Whether the Autopilot profile indicates Hybrid Azure AD Join (CloudAssignedDomainJoinMethod == 1). Derived from the profile at registration time.

fields.name: isSelfDeployingProfile
fields.doc: Whether the Autopilot profile carries the self-deploying/kiosk OOBE marker (CloudAssignedOobeConfig bits 0x20|0x40; validated platform-wide 2026-07-02 as exclusive to self-deploying profiles). Display/filter metadata only — the DecisionCore behavioural gate consumes the EnrollmentFactsObserved signal, not this flag.

fields.name: isCloudPc
fields.doc: Whether the agent identified the device as a Windows 365 Cloud PC (marker AND: HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows365 key + installed CloudManagedDesktopExtension service — the evidence set field-verified by bootstrap v2.3-dev.2). Display/filter metadata only, agent-reported and NOT server-verified; the authoritative Cloud PC auth signal is ValidatedBy == CloudPc (cert-CN-bound Graph lookup). The two can legitimately disagree, e.g. when a Cloud PC is admitted via Autopilot validation.

fields.name: validatedBy
fields.doc: Which backend device-validation path accepted this registration (Autopilot S/N, Corporate Identifier, Device Association, or Bootstrap token). SERVER-POPULATED: RegisterSessionFunction overwrites this unconditionally from its own SecurityValidationResult — any agent-sent value is ignored.

SessionReportDownloadUrlResponse.doc: Success body of GET global/session-reports/download-url: short-lived SAS download URL for a session report blob.

SessionReportListResponse.doc: Success body of GET global/session-reports — both the non-paged and the paged variant (the non-paged variant simply carries no nextLink; WhenWritingNull keeps the wire identical to the historical shape).

fields.name: nextLink
fields.doc: Absolute-path link to the next page; null/absent on the last page and in non-paged responses.

SessionReportMetadata.doc: Session report metadata for the admin-config reports table. Both Session-context reports and Diag-Files-only reports share this row schema — the ReportType discriminator distinguishes the two, and SessionId is empty for diag-files submissions.

fields.name: reportType
fields.doc: One of ReportTypes. Defaults to "session" so legacy rows map cleanly.

fields.name: diagnosticsBlobName
fields.doc: Flat name of the session diagnostics archive copied into the session-reports container at submit time. Null when the copy was never requested or failed.

fields.name: diagnosticsCopyStatus
fields.doc: Outcome of the diagnostics copy: "Copied" or one of the "Failed:*" reasons. Null when the submitter did not request the copy.

SessionRestoreResponse.doc: Body of POST global/sessions/{id}/restore for every outcome (success AND reject — the outcome/status mapping decides the HTTP code, the shape stays one).

fields.name: outcome
fields.doc: SessionRestoreOutcome name (e.g. "Restored", "DryRunOk", "RejectManifestNotFound").

fields.name: mode
fields.doc: "full" | "partial" | "dryRun"; absent on early rejects.

fields.name: message
fields.doc: Operator-readable reason; absent on clean successes.

fields.name: currentState
fields.doc: Reject diagnostics; absent otherwise.

fields.name: pendingManifestId
fields.doc: Reject diagnostics; absent otherwise.

SessionStats.doc: Aggregated session counters for the dashboard stats cards. Computed server-side over a windowed scan of the SessionsIndex so the numbers don't drift with whatever the client happens to have paginated into memory.

fields.name: days
fields.doc: Window the windowed counters were computed over (matches request).

fields.name: activeCount
fields.doc: InProgress sessions inside the window. Used for the "Active Sessions" card.

fields.name: totalLastNDays
fields.doc: Total sessions started inside the window.

fields.name: incompleteLastNDays
fields.doc: Terminal, non-failure sessions in the window (tasks/enrollment-status-reclassification.md): the sweep saw no completion or explicit failure. Reported as the third headline bucket and deliberately excluded from SuccessRatePct (which is over Succeeded + Failed only).

fields.name: successRatePct
fields.doc: Succeeded / (Succeeded + Failed) * 100, rounded. Zero when no terminal sessions are in the window (the card renders "0%" rather than NaN).

fields.name: avgDurationMinutes
fields.doc: Average duration of Succeeded sessions in the window, in minutes (rounded). Kept for API compatibility; the dashboard card leads with the median, which multi-hour outliers cannot drag around.

fields.name: medianDurationMinutes
fields.doc: Median duration in minutes over the same Succeeded population.

fields.name: p90DurationMinutes
fields.doc: 90th-percentile duration in minutes over the same population — the tail signal.

fields.name: totalToday
fields.doc: Sessions whose StartedAt is on or after UTC midnight of the current day.

fields.name: computedAt
fields.doc: UTC timestamp of when the snapshot was produced (server clock).

SessionStatsResponse.doc: Dashboard stats envelope shared by GetSessionStats and GetAllSessionStats.

fields.name: quotaExcludedTenants
fields.doc: See QuotaExcludedTenants; only GetAllSessionStats ever sets it.

fields.name: failureSource
fields.doc: Origin of a Failed status — persisted ONLY on a Failed write (a non-Failed verdict discards it; see VerdictPath for the status-independent attribution). Values: - "" / null: agent-reported (default; terminal enrollment_failed event) - "rule:<RuleId>": session failed because an analyze rule with MarkSessionAsFailed fired - "manual": operator flipped the session via the portal - "max_lifetime_watchdog": the agent's max-lifetime shutdown verdict was Failed Consumers use this to render rule-based failures distinctly (badge + link to rule).

fields.name: verdictPath
fields.doc: Machine-readable origin of the CURRENT Status — which code path wrote it (VerdictPaths vocabulary, e.g. agent:complete, sweep:r5_incomplete, manual:failed). Stamped on every status write regardless of status, so the verdict calibration aggregate can count each path. Null on rows written before instrumentation (read-side derivation covers those).

fields.name: priorStatus
fields.doc: The verdict this session carried BEFORE the current status overrode it — set only when a write replaces a prior Succeeded/Failed/Incomplete/AwaitingUser (admin mark, late agent completion upgrading a sweep verdict, retro-reclassification). Together with PriorVerdictPath this is the correction stream: "path X was overridden". Null when the status never overrode a verdict.

fields.name: priorVerdictPath
fields.doc: The VerdictPath of the overridden prior verdict; see PriorStatus.

fields.name: reconcileReason
fields.doc: Non-empty only when the BACKEND (not the agent) declared this session Succeeded: either the maintenance timeout sweep reconciled it (e.g. "user completed setup — desktop + Windows Hello observed") or a late completion report upgraded a prior Failed/Incomplete/AwaitingUser verdict. Carries the human-readable justification so operators can always tell a backend-declared success from an agent-reported one. Admin-marked successes are attributed via AdminMarkedAction instead and leave this empty.

fields.name: espSoftFailure
fields.doc: True only on a Succeeded session that completed while an ESP-failure advisory was still unresolved: the ESP demonstrably gave up on at least one blocking item (typically the 30-min timeout wall) and the user most likely pressed "Continue anyway" — the device reached a working desktop, but not everything the ESP tracked finished inside its window. Rendered as the amber "completed with issues" badge. False/absent = clean success.

fields.name: completionSource
fields.doc: How a soft-failure completion was detected. Values: - "continue_anyway_observation": Device-phase ESP failure, tenant opted into the Continue-Anyway observation window, real-user desktop arrived inside it - "continue_anyway_post_accountsetup": classic advisory defang (AccountSetup had already been entered when the ESP failure fired) Empty on clean successes.

fields.name: adminMarkedAction
fields.doc: Non-null only when an administrator explicitly flipped the session via the portal (MarkSessionSucceeded / MarkSessionFailed). Values: null (default, agent-driven), "Succeeded", "Failed". This is the authoritative source for the backend's AdminAction response field sent to agents. Previously the backend inferred admin-override from "status is terminal + current event is not a completion marker", which fired falsely on every post-completion event the agent sent (agent_shutting_down, diagnostics_uploaded, enrollment_summary_shown). The dedicated field eliminates that false-positive.

fields.name: validatedBy
fields.doc: Which backend device-validation path accepted this device at session registration — ValidatorType name as string: "AutopilotV1" (Autopilot S/N lookup), "CorporateIdentifier", "DeviceAssociation" (device preparation), "CloudPc", or "Bootstrap" (pre-MDM token). Latest non-Unknown validation wins (a Bootstrap session re-registering under cert auth upgrades to the cert-path validator). Empty for sessions that predate this field or tenants with device validation off.

fields.name: avgApiLatencyMs
fields.doc: Session-wide average HTTP round-trip latency (ms) of the agent's calls to the backend API, as measured on the device (includes network RTT + TLS + server processing). Projected at ingest from the cumulative counters of the latest agent_metrics_snapshot (net_total_latency_ms / net_total_requests). Null for V1 sessions and sessions from agents that predate the field. Aggregate across sessions weighted by ApiRequestCount — e.g. per GeoCountry to compare regional backend reachability.

fields.name: apiRequestCount
fields.doc: Number of HTTP requests behind AvgApiLatencyMs (the cumulative net_total_requests at the latest snapshot). Needed as the weight when averaging latency across sessions. Null whenever AvgApiLatencyMs is.

fields.name: connectionType
fields.doc: Active network connection type during enrollment: "WiFi" or "Ethernet". Projected at ingest from the latest network_interface_info event (last emission wins — a device that switches media mid-enrollment reports the most recent state). Null for sessions that predate the projection.

fields.name: enrollmentType
fields.doc: Enrollment type: "v1" (Autopilot Classic/ESP) or "v2" (Windows Device Preparation). Defaults to "v1" for sessions that predate this field.

fields.name: diagnosticsBlobName
fields.doc: Blob name of the uploaded diagnostics archive (null if not uploaded). Used to construct a download URL. Path semantics depend on : CustomerSas: blob name only (e.g. AgentDiagnostics-...zip); download builds the URL from the tenant's container SAS.Hosted: full path including the {tenantId}/ prefix (e.g. {tenantId}/AgentDiagnostics-...zip); download streams directly via the backend connection string.

fields.name: diagnosticsBlobDestination
fields.doc: Where the diagnostics archive for THIS session was uploaded. Frozen at upload time so the download path can route correctly even if the tenant later switches DiagnosticsUploadDestination. "CustomerSas" — blob lives in the customer's storage; download uses the tenant's SAS URL (current behaviour)."Hosted" — blob lives in the backend's storage under {tenantId}/; download streams via the Functions connection string.null (legacy rows that predate this field) — treated as "CustomerSas" by the download path for back-compat.

fields.name: lastEventAt
fields.doc: Timestamp of the most recently received event for this session. Updated on every event batch ingestion. Used by maintenance to detect sessions that are still actively sending data beyond the configured window. Null for sessions that predate this field.

fields.name: lastIngestAt
fields.doc: SERVER-side time of the most recent event ingest for this session. lives in the DEVICE clock frame (it is the maximum agent-supplied event timestamp). Comparing it against a server-derived cutoff mixes two clock frames: a device whose clock runs slow — or one whose IME-derived events carry a timezone skew — is judged silent far too early or not at all (measured in the field: skews from -17 h to +1 h, see tasks/todo.md). This field is stamped from the server clock on every ingest, so silence detection can compare like with like. Null for sessions that predate this field — callers MUST fall back to LastEventAt so rollout has no blind window.

fields.name: isPreProvisioned
fields.doc: Whether this session used WhiteGlove (Pre-Provisioning). Set when a whiteglove_complete event is processed.

fields.name: resumedAt
fields.doc: Timestamp when the WhiteGlove session resumed for user enrollment (Part 2). Set when the agent sends a whiteglove_resumed event or re-registers from Pending state. Used to compute the user enrollment duration (Duration 2) for Teams notifications.

fields.name: stalledAt
fields.doc: Timestamp when the session was marked as Stalled. Set when the agent sends a session_stalled event (after 60 min without progress) or when the backend 2h maintenance sweep detects agent silence. Cleared (null) when the session heals back to InProgress via a new real event.

fields.name: isHybridJoin
fields.doc: Whether the Autopilot profile indicates Hybrid Azure AD Join. Derived from CloudAssignedDomainJoinMethod == 1 in the Autopilot profile.

fields.name: isSelfDeployingProfile
fields.doc: Whether the Autopilot profile carries the self-deploying/kiosk OOBE marker (CloudAssignedOobeConfig bits 0x20|0x40). Sent by the agent at registration; sticky-true across re-registrations.

fields.name: isCloudPc
fields.doc: Whether the agent identified the device as a Windows 365 Cloud PC (Windows365 registry key + CloudManagedDesktopExtension service, marker AND). Sent by the agent at registration; sticky-true across re-registrations. Agent-reported context — independent of ValidatedBy == CloudPc, which is the server-derived cert-CN-bound Graph verification.

fields.name: rebootCount
fields.doc: Number of system reboots observed during the enrollment. Counts the agent's system_reboot_detected events (V2 only — one per reboot, detected via the System event-log boot time on the next agent start). Maintained incrementally per ingest batch for a live value, then overwritten with an authoritative distinct count from the Events table when the session reaches a terminal status (self-corrects any at-least-once batch double-count). 0 for V1 sessions and sessions that predate this field.

fields.name: excessiveEventsAlerted
fields.doc: True once maintenance has emitted an ExcessiveSessionEvents ops alert for this session. Prevents duplicate alerts on subsequent maintenance runs for the same runaway session.

fields.name: excessiveEventsAutoActioned
fields.doc: True once maintenance has auto-blocked or auto-killed the device for this runaway session (see ExcessiveEventAutoActionMode). Independent of ExcessiveEventsAlerted so warn and auto-action are each idempotent on their own — admins can change the auto-action mode mid-flight without re-firing the warn.

fields.name: pendingActionsJson
fields.doc: JSON-serialized List`1 of ServerAction pending delivery to the agent. Empty string when no actions are queued. The Ingest function reads this alongside the session's status fields (no extra I/O), attaches the actions to the response, and clears the column via a merge.

fields.name: pendingActionsQueuedAt
fields.doc: When the first pending action was queued. Used for TTL and staleness detection — maintenance can purge actions older than a threshold to prevent zombie signals on long-dead sessions.

fields.name: failureSnapshotJson
fields.doc: Compact JSON snapshot of "last known session state" written by the maintenance 5h-timeout sweep when a session graduates to terminal Failed (Hybrid User-Driven completion-gap fix, 2026-05-01). Captures the canonical lifecycle anchors — last ESP phase, desktop arrival, Hello policy, AAD-join state, missing signals — so operators don't have to scroll through hundreds of events to reconstruct where a stuck session was when the watchdog fired. Empty / null on healthy-completion paths and on sessions that predate the field. Built by FailureSnapshotBuilder.

fields.name: deletionState
fields.doc: Cascade-delete state-machine value (Plan §1 P7 / PR3). One of SessionDeletionState constants. Empty / null means no cascade in flight (legacy rows; treated as None). Written to the primary Sessions table only — the deletion CAS path does not sync SessionsIndex, so this is NOT part of the index mirror today and is read on the truth-served detail/guard paths. Mirroring it into SessionsIndex (so list/search can flag locked sessions) is a deferred follow-up.

fields.name: pendingDeletionManifestId
fields.doc: ULID of the in-flight cascade manifest when DeletionState is non-None. Used by the producer to detect concurrent re-enqueues (same ManifestId → resume, different ManifestId → 409 Conflict). Null otherwise.

SessionTimeBreakdown.doc: Per-session enrollment time attribution (F1, insights spec) — an exact partition of the session's authoritative wall clock into named segments plus an explicit unattributed remainder. Invariant (unit-enforced): sum of all span seconds + UnattributedSeconds == WallClockSeconds == the session's DurationSeconds (which excludes the WhiteGlove pause by design — never CompletedAt − StartedAt, which diverges in 25 % of terminal sessions). Computed once at session-terminal processing by TimeAttributionCalculator; persisted in SessionTimeBreakdowns (F1 PR2).

fields.name: attributionVersion
fields.doc: Attribution algorithm version — a definition change bumps this so aggregates never silently mix semantics (truthfulness rule 8).

fields.name: eventCountAtCompute
fields.doc: The session's EventCount when this breakdown was computed — the maintenance sweep's change signal: late or replayed event batches move the session's count, so a mismatch means the row was computed from an incomplete stream and gets recomputed (Codex review: the inline terminal compute is one-shot). 0 = row written before this column existed → recomputed once by the next sweep.

fields.name: wallClockSeconds
fields.doc: The session's authoritative DurationSeconds at compute time.

fields.name: segments
fields.doc: Attributed spans, ordered by StartUtc. Multiple spans may share a segment key.

fields.name: unattributedSeconds
fields.doc: Exact remainder: WallClockSeconds − sum of span seconds.

fields.name: rebootSeconds
fields.doc: Total observed reboot outage seconds. Cross-cutting annotation — reboots overlap the segments they occur in and are NOT part of the wall-clock partition.

fields.name: sleepSeconds
fields.doc: Total observed in-window sleep seconds. Cross-cutting annotation like RebootSeconds — the wall clock keeps the pause; this discloses it.

fields.name: blockingApps
fields.doc: Install intervals of ESP-blocking apps (positive-evidence join against the latest esp_config_detected lists), top 20 by duration. BlockingAppCount carries the uncapped count of matched blocking apps (including those without a measurable interval, e.g. unobserved start).

fields.name: blockingAppCount
fields.doc: Uncapped count of apps matched against the blocking set (see BlockingApps).

fields.name: espAppsOccupancySeconds
fields.doc: Overlap-merged union of the blocking-app intervals clipped to the esp_apps spans — the critical-path occupancy. esp_apps total − occupancy = in-phase wait (provider stalls, settle, IME idle). Null when the blocking set is unknown (no lists observed): unknown, not zero.

SetMcpUserUsagePlanResponse.doc: Response of PATCH global/mcp-users/{upn}/usage-plan: the UPN and the plan now in effect ("(inherit)" when cleared to the tenant default).

SetTenantPlanTierResponse.doc: Response of PATCH config/{tenantId}/plan: the resulting plan/trial state.

fields.name: effectiveEdition
fields.doc: Effective edition after the change, lowercase ("community" | "pro").

fields.name: editionSource
fields.doc: Source of the effective edition: "community" | "plan" | "trial" | "msp" (conferred by the managing tenant).

fields.name: retentionGraceEndsUtc
fields.doc: End of the retention downgrade grace window, or null — the key is omitted when null.

fields.name: maxDelegatedTenants
fields.doc: Effective delegated (MSP) tenant slot limit after the change (override or plan entitlement).

fields.name: maxDelegatedTenantsOverride
fields.doc: The Global Admin override; omitted when the plan entitlement applies.

fields.name: mcpUsagePlan
fields.doc: Effective MCP usage plan name of the tenant after the change (override or edition default).

fields.name: mcpUsagePlanOverride
fields.doc: The Global Admin MCP usage-plan override (a SectionUsagePlans plan name); omitted when the edition default applies.

fields.name: payingCustomer
fields.doc: Sales bookkeeping: whether the tenant pays for its plan. No entitlement effect.

SetUsagePlanRequest.doc: Body of PATCH global/mcp-users/{upn}/usage-plan; null clears the override.

SeverityBreakdown.doc: Distinct-CVE counts grouped by their highest CVSS severity band.

fields.name: serialNumber
fields.doc: Serial-number knowledge proof for session-group joins. Required only for roleless same-tenant callers (Progress Portal end users); member, Global Admin and delegated callers never need to send it.

SignalRNegotiateResponse.doc: Response of POST realtime/negotiate: exactly the shape the @microsoft/signalr client's negotiate protocol expects.

SlaMetricsResponse.doc: SLA metrics response for a given tenant and time window.

fields.name: currentWeek
fields.doc: Current ISO week SLA snapshot.

fields.name: weeklyTrend
fields.doc: Weekly trend (newest first).

fields.name: violators
fields.doc: Sessions that breached SLA targets (failed or exceeded duration).

fields.name: appInstallSla
fields.doc: App install SLA snapshot (null if no app install target configured).

SlaSnapshot.doc: SLA compliance snapshot for a single period (ISO week).

fields.name: week
fields.doc: ISO week identifier, e.g. "2026-W15".

fields.name: durationViolationCount
fields.doc: Number of sessions that exceeded the duration target.

fields.name: successRateMet
fields.doc: Whether the success rate target is met.

fields.name: durationTargetMet
fields.doc: Whether the P95 duration target is met.

SlaViolatorSession.doc: A session that violated SLA targets.

fields.name: violationType
fields.doc: "Failed", "DurationExceeded", or "Both".

SlaWeeklyTrend.doc: SLA compliance trend entry for one ISO week.

fields.name: week
fields.doc: ISO week identifier, e.g. "2026-W15".

SleepSpan.doc: One completed sleep episode observed during the session (system_sleep_episode payload — enteredAt/exitedAt are the authoritative instants, never the event's own timestamp, which is stamped at wake and may be clamped). Cross-cutting annotation like RebootSpan: sleep overlaps the segment it started in and is NOT part of the wall-clock partition — the session really took that long; the span explains where the time went.

fields.name: segmentKey
fields.doc: Segment the episode started in (TimeAttributionSegments key, or "unattributed").

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: Episode kind from the agent payload: "sleep", "hibernate" or "modern_standby".

SoftwareInventoryResponse.doc: Shared response of GET vulnerability/software-inventory (Global Admin, ?tenantId=) and GET metrics/software-inventory (caller's own tenant): the raw SoftwareInventory rows plus matched/unmatched counts. Consumed by the MCP get_software_inventory tool — key names are part of that contract.

fields.name: inventory
fields.doc: Raw SoftwareInventory table rows, serialized verbatim under their storage column keys.

StartTenantTrialResponse.doc: Response of POST config/{tenantId}/trial: the started self-service trial.

fields.name: effectiveEdition
fields.doc: Always the Pro tier name — starting a trial makes the tenant effectively Pro.

SubmitDiagFilesReportRequest.doc: Request to submit diagnostic files for analysis without a session context. Used from /settings/tenant/support when an admin needs to ship logs/state files to the Autopilot Monitor team without binding them to a specific enrollment session.

fields.name: screenshotBase64
fields.doc: Base64-encoded screenshot image (optional)

fields.name: screenshotFileName
fields.doc: Original screenshot file name for extension detection

fields.name: agentLogBase64
fields.doc: Base64-encoded log/state payload (single file or zip of many; max ~5 MB enforced client-side)

fields.name: agentLogFileName
fields.doc: Original file name (e.g. "agent.log", "state.json", "diag-files.zip")

SubmitSessionReportRequest.doc: Request to submit a session report for analysis by the Autopilot Monitor team. Sent as JSON from the frontend; the backend creates the ZIP and uploads to central storage.

fields.name: sessionCsv
fields.doc: Session row as CSV (single data row with header)

fields.name: timelineExportTxt
fields.doc: Pre-generated UI timeline export (TXT)

fields.name: eventsCsv
fields.doc: Pre-generated raw events table export (CSV)

fields.name: ruleResultsCsv
fields.doc: Pre-generated analysis rule results export (CSV)

fields.name: screenshotBase64
fields.doc: Base64-encoded screenshot image (optional)

fields.name: screenshotFileName
fields.doc: Original screenshot file name for extension detection

fields.name: agentLogBase64
fields.doc: Base64-encoded agent log file (optional, max 5 MB)

fields.name: agentLogFileName
fields.doc: Original agent log file name

fields.name: includeDiagnostics
fields.doc: When true and the session has an uploaded diagnostics archive, the backend copies that archive server-side into the durable session-reports container so it survives session deletion and retention cleanup.

fields.name: exportedEventCount
fields.doc: Number of events the client had loaded when it generated the exports.

fields.name: sessionEventCount
fields.doc: The session's EventCount as the client saw it — compared against ExportedEventCount this flags a partial export.

fields.name: eventStreamActive
fields.doc: True when the client was still streaming event pages at submit time.

SuccessMessageResponse.doc: Canonical mutation acknowledgement: { "success": ..., "message": ... }. No property defaults on purpose — every call site sets both, and a default would add a key the anonymous site never wrote.

SuppressByEventConfig.doc: Configuration for suppressing a condition match when a "resolving" event exists. Example: suppress an app_install_failed match when app_install_completed exists for the same appId.

fields.name: eventType
fields.doc: The event type that resolves/suppresses the matched event (e.g., "app_install_completed").

fields.name: joinField
fields.doc: The data field to join on — must have the same value in both the matched event and the suppressing event (e.g., "appId").

TelemetryItemDto.doc: The wire shape of one telemetry item sent by the V2 agent to POST /api/agent/telemetry (Plan §2.7a / §M5). This class IS the contract on both ends: the agent maps its ctor-validated, immutable TelemetryItem through TelemetryItem.ToWire() and serialises a list of these; the ingest deserialises the same class. Two tests pin it — the agent's TelemetryWireContractTests (round trip plus the frozen body under tests/fixtures/telemetry-wire/) and the backend's TelemetryWireFixtureTests (every frozen body must dispatch with zero rejections). Serialisation: Newtonsoft.Json defaults on both sides — PascalCase member names, ISO-8601 UTC dates, as the name. A value the ingest cannot route or parse is answered with 422 + a poison body naming the RowKeys (), never dropped silently.

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: TelemetryItemKind name — routes to the destination table. Kept as a string on the wire so an unknown value fails ONE item (poison), not the whole batch.

fields.name: partitionKey
fields.doc: Azure-Table PartitionKey, typically {tenantId}_{sessionId}.

fields.name: telemetryItemId
fields.doc: Transport-cursor — monotonic per session across all item kinds.

fields.name: sessionTraceOrdinal
fields.doc: Null for agent-global items (no session).

fields.name: payloadJson
fields.doc: Already-serialised JSON of the wrapped payload (EnrollmentEvent / DecisionSignal / DecisionTransition).

TelemetryItemKind.doc: Kind of a telemetry item on the agent → backend wire (POST /api/agent/telemetry). One vocabulary for both ends: the agent's spool and TelemetryItem.ToWire() write the enum NAME ("Event", "Signal", "DecisionTransition"), the ingest routes by TelemetryItemKind@). Names are the contract — never the ordinal — so a future member can be appended without touching the routing of existing agents (L.14). Three destination tables: → Events (full event pipeline), → Signals, → DecisionTransitions.

TelemetryItemsRejectedResponse.doc: 422 body of agent/telemetry when one or more items of a batch cannot be routed (unknown Kind) or parsed (unusable payload). This is the backend end of the agent's poison protocol: Poison plus a non-empty RejectedRowKeys authorise the agent to drop exactly those items and re-upload the rest of the batch; NOTHING of the batch was stored. Without this body the agent retains the batch forever (a bare 4xx never infers poison) — and before it existed the ingest answered 200 and the items were lost when the agent cleared its spool.

fields.name: poison
fields.doc: Always true — the flag the agent's poison parser requires.

fields.name: rejectedRowKeys
fields.doc: RowKeys of the rejected items, batch order; the agent drops exactly these.

fields.name: reason
fields.doc: Compact per-cause summary for the agent's poison report, e.g. unknown_kind=1;unparseable=2.

fields.name: received
fields.doc: Items in the batch.

fields.name: rejected
fields.doc: Items named in RejectedRowKeys.

TemplateVariable.doc: Defines a template variable in a rule condition that must be customized per-tenant. Points at a specific condition field (by index) and describes what value the user needs to provide.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Machine name for this variable (e.g., "cert_subject")

fields.name: label
fields.doc: Human-readable label shown in the configuration UI (e.g., "Certificate Subject")

fields.name: description
fields.doc: Help text explaining what value the user should provide

fields.name: conditionIndex
fields.doc: Zero-based index into the rule's Conditions array where this variable lives

fields.name: field
fields.doc: Which field on the condition to customize: "value", "eventType", "dataField", "eventAFilterValue"

fields.name: placeholder
fields.doc: The placeholder value that ships with the template (e.g., "CN=YOUR-CERTIFICATE-SUBJECT")

fields.name: validation
fields.doc: Optional regex pattern to validate user input

TenantAdminCreatedResponse.doc: Response of POST tenants/{tenantId}/admins: the created tenant member.

TenantAdminRow.doc: One tenant member (Admin / Operator / Viewer) on the wire — the item of the bare-array GET tenants/{tenantId}/admins and the created member of the POST. Deliberately NOT the storage entity: the ITableEntity keys (partitionKey/rowKey/eTag/timestamp) that the pre-2026-08-31 wire carried are storage internals and were dropped from the contract (no consumer read them).

fields.name: tenantId
fields.doc: Tenant ID (lowercase).

fields.name: upn
fields.doc: User Principal Name (lowercase).

fields.name: role
fields.doc: Role: "Admin", "Operator", "Viewer". A null (legacy pre-role row) omits the key and means Admin.

fields.name: canManageBootstrapTokens
fields.doc: Whether this Operator can manage bootstrap tokens (only relevant for Operator).

TenantConfigBackupItem.doc: One pre-write config snapshot in GET config/{tenantId}/backups — metadata only, the raw EntityJson (clear-text secrets) is never returned.

fields.name: backupId
fields.doc: The snapshot's RowKey (reverse-ticks + short guid) — the public backup id.

fields.name: source
fields.doc: Write path that triggered the snapshot (portal-put | plan | mcp-patch | ...).

fields.name: reason
fields.doc: Caller-provided intent, or null — the key is omitted when null.

fields.name: diff
fields.doc: Masked "old → new" change summary, or null when unparseable — the key is omitted when null.

TenantConfigFieldSchema.doc: One entry of the tenant-config field schema (built by TenantConfigPatchService.BuildFieldsSchema). Serialized camelCase; null Format/Reason keys are omitted (WhenWritingNull) — the null and set cases are pinned by ConfigWireParityTests.

TenantConfigPatchFailedResponse.doc: Error body of PATCH config/{tenantId}/fields when the patch was not applied (400/404/409/503/500): envelope prefix plus the pre-write backup id and, on a rolled-back write, the fields that drifted.

fields.name: backupId
fields.doc: Pre-write snapshot id when a backup was taken before the failure; absent otherwise.

fields.name: drift
fields.doc: Fields whose post-write read-back differed from the intent (rolled back); absent otherwise.

fields.name: diff
fields.doc: Masked "old → new" summary, or null — the key is omitted when null.

fields.name: backupId
fields.doc: Pre-write snapshot id, or null (no-op writes take no backup) — the key is omitted when null.

fields.name: noOp
fields.doc: True when the patch changed nothing (zero applied fields).

TenantConfiguration.doc: Tenant-specific configuration stored in Azure Table Storage PartitionKey = TenantId RowKey = "config"

fields.name: tenantId
fields.doc: Tenant ID (PartitionKey in Table Storage)

fields.name: domainName
fields.doc: Domain name extracted from the first user's UPN Used for display purposes (e.g., contoso.com)

fields.name: lastUpdated
fields.doc: When the configuration was last updated

fields.name: updatedBy
fields.doc: Updated by (user email or system)

fields.name: onboardedBy
fields.doc: UPN of the user whose first login created this tenant configuration. Set once in HandleNewTenantDomainAsync alongside DomainName and never overwritten. Used by the preview-approval auto-promote path so background jobs that mutate UpdatedBy (e.g. global rate-limit sync) cannot leak a sentinel string into the TenantAdmins table. Null on rows that pre-date the OnboardedBy field — auto-promote falls back to UpdatedBy with a UPN-shape guard.

fields.name: contactEmail
fields.doc: Address used to reach this tenant about the service itself — a technical problem, a security matter, or a change that needs an administrator's attention. Editable by the tenant's own admins under Settings → Tenant → Contact. Seeded once at onboarding from the tenant's notification address if one was given, and never re-synced afterwards: from that point the value belongs to the tenant, and a later edit must not be overwritten by the onboarding source. Purpose-limited by design — service communication only. It is never used for marketing and never disclosed. Null means we have no way to reach this tenant, which is why enforcement actions cannot promise prior warning.

fields.name: companyName
fields.doc: Organization name behind this tenant, as the tenant's admins want it read by a support engineer — the counterpart of ContactEmail in the tenant's contact profile. Editable under Settings → Tenant → Contact. Optional on Community. Together with it is required at the self-service Pro entry point (trial start) so a paying tenant is reachable and identifiable for support; it is never a runtime gate on Pro features, and a GA plan assignment does not require it (the admin UI warns instead). Never derived from : the domain is a technical label, the company name is what the tenant tells us. Null means not provided.

fields.name: onboardedAt
fields.doc: When this tenant was first onboarded (derived from earliest TenantAdmin AddedDate). Used for feedback eligibility checks (tenant must be old enough before prompting). Backfilled by the maintenance job for existing tenants; set to UtcNow for new tenants.

fields.name: homedAppClientId
fields.doc: Client id of the Entra app registration this tenant is homed on. Drives which app mints Graph client-credential tokens and admin-consent URLs for the tenant, and which app the portal signs the tenant's users in with (via the auth/me "homedApp" field). Null = the legacy (pre-migration) app registration — the invariant for every tenant onboarded before the C4A8 move. Set to the primary client id at onboarding when the first login arrived via the primary app; flipped by a Global Admin after a tenant re-consents to the new app (GA-only field, see UpdateTenantConfigurationFunction).

fields.name: lastAuthClientId
fields.doc: Client id observed in the most recent portal login token's audience — pure observability for the app-reg migration (which app a tenant's users actually arrive through), never used for routing decisions. Written on change only.

fields.name: lastAuthClientIdSince
fields.doc: When LastAuthClientId last changed (i.e. logins arrive via that app since this instant). Null on rows that pre-date the field.

fields.name: disabled
fields.doc: Whether this tenant is disabled/suspended If true, users from this tenant cannot log in Default: false

fields.name: disabledReason
fields.doc: Optional reason why the tenant was disabled Displayed to users attempting to log in

fields.name: disabledUntil
fields.doc: Optional date/time until which the tenant is disabled If set and in the past, the tenant can be automatically re-enabled If null, the tenant remains disabled until manually re-enabled

fields.name: customRateLimitRequestsPerMinute
fields.doc: Optional per-tenant override for the device (agent/cert) API rate limit. If null, the effective limit is the global AdminConfiguration.GlobalRateLimitRequestsPerMinute. If set, this value takes precedence. Global-Admin-only (see UpdateTenantConfigurationFunction GA-gate).

fields.name: customUserRateLimitRequestsPerMinute
fields.doc: Optional per-tenant override for the user (portal/JWT) API rate limit applied to standard users (Tenant Admins, Operators, Viewers). If null, the effective limit is the global AdminConfiguration.UserRateLimitRequestsPerMinute. Global-Admin-only. Note: Global Admins are rate-limited by the global GlobalAdminRateLimitRequestsPerMinute (cross-tenant), so this override does not apply to them.

fields.name: planTier
fields.doc: Tenant plan tier. Determines default API rate limits and feature gates. Write-side values: "community", "pro". The legacy stored values "enterprise" (resolves to Pro) and "free" (resolves to Community) remain readable — see FeatureEntitlementCatalog. Managed by Global Admins.

fields.name: trialExpiresUtc
fields.doc: End of the tenant's Pro trial (UTC). While this is in the future the tenant's effective edition is Pro regardless of PlanTier. Null = no trial. Expiry degrades the tenant to Community at read time — no timer involved.

fields.name: trialStartedUtc
fields.doc: When the tenant's Pro trial was started (UTC). Informational/audit only.

fields.name: trialConsumed
fields.doc: Whether the tenant has used its one self-service trial. Once true, further trials can only be granted by a Global Admin via the plan management endpoint (which does not reset this flag).

fields.name: trialGrantedBy
fields.doc: Who granted/started the trial (UPN of the self-service caller or the Global Admin).

fields.name: proDowngradedUtc
fields.doc: When the tenant's EFFECTIVE edition last dropped Pro → Community via the plan endpoint (UTC). Anchors the retention downgrade grace period: for RetentionDowngradeGraceDays after losing Pro the retention cap stays at the Pro value so a downgrade (e.g. non-payment) does not immediately hard-delete data older than the Community cap. Trial expiry needs no write — TrialExpiresUtc itself is the anchor there. Cleared whenever the tenant becomes effectively Pro again. Backend-only: not delivered to the agent (no ConfigVersion impact).

fields.name: maxDelegatedTenantsOverride
fields.doc: Global-Admin override of the delegated ("MSP") tenant slot limit — how many distinct customer tenants users homed in this tenant may manage. Null = the plan entitlement applies (Community 0, Pro 2); a value applies regardless of edition (pre-provisioning a package), while USING delegation still requires Pro. Mutable only via the plan endpoint. Backend-only: not delivered to the agent (no ConfigVersion impact).

fields.name: mcpUsagePlanOverride
fields.doc: Global-Admin override of the tenant's MCP usage plan — the NAME of a SectionUsagePlans plan (AdminConfiguration.PlanTierDefinitionsJson), e.g. "msp". Applies to the WHOLE tenant: every member's default user plan (a per-user McpUsers override still wins) AND the organization-wide windows. Null/blank = the edition default (community/pro). Does NOT change the edition — Pro feature gates stay on PlanTier. Mutable only via the plan endpoint (validated against the plan definitions there). Backend-only: not delivered to the agent (no ConfigVersion impact).

fields.name: payingCustomer
fields.doc: Sales/support bookkeeping: whether this tenant PAYS for its plan (as opposed to a Pro tier assigned by support, a trial, or Pro conferred by a managing tenant). Carries NO entitlement — the effective edition is resolved from PlanTier/TrialExpiresUtc/ManagedByProTenantId only. Mutable only via the plan endpoint (Global Admin); shown in the operator tenant list, never in feature flags or any customer-facing surface. Backend-only: not delivered to the agent (no ConfigVersion impact).

fields.name: managedByProTenantId
fields.doc: READ-TIME PROJECTION, NEVER STORED: the permanent-Pro tenant that currently manages this tenant through a self-service delegation (member of that tenant's owned msp-{tid} Tenant Group), or null. Populated by the backend's configuration loader on every read path from the Tenant Groups index; the table repository has no column for it and the patch endpoint denies it. While set, the tenant's effective edition is Pro with source "msp" (no delegation right of its own) — the delegation ending, the managing tenant losing its permanent Pro tier, or its offboarding all revert this automatically because nothing is written here. Not delivered to the agent (no ConfigVersion impact).

fields.name: manufacturerWhitelist
fields.doc: Hardware whitelist: Allowed manufacturers (supports wildcards like "Dell*") Comma-separated list

fields.name: modelWhitelist
fields.doc: Hardware whitelist: Allowed models (supports wildcards like "Latitude*") Comma-separated list Default: "*" (all models allowed)

fields.name: validateAutopilotDevice
fields.doc: Whether to validate devices against Intune Autopilot device registration Requires Graph API integration (admin consent for DeviceManagementServiceConfig.Read.All)

fields.name: validateCorporateIdentifier
fields.doc: Whether to validate devices against Intune Corporate Device Identifiers (manufacturer + model + serial number via importedDeviceIdentities/searchExistingIdentities). Requires Graph API integration (admin consent for DeviceManagementServiceConfig.ReadWrite.All)

fields.name: validateDeviceAssociation
fields.doc: Whether to validate devices against the Windows Autopilot device preparation "Device association" catalog via Graph (tenantAssociatedDevices, serial number match). One of the accepting methods of the device-validation gate, evaluated after the Autopilot and Corporate Identifier lookups (see SecurityValidator). Device association is GA since 2026-08-25; associated devices are marked corporate-owned by Intune itself, so no corporate identifier exists for them. Requires the same Graph permission as the other validators (DeviceManagementServiceConfig.Read.All).

fields.name: validateCloudPcDevice
fields.doc: Whether to validate Windows 365 Cloud PCs as a fallback when the Autopilot / Corporate Identifier lookups miss. Cloud PCs are provisioned by the Windows 365 service and are structurally never Autopilot-registered; this validator instead resolves the Intune device id from the (chain-validated) MDM client certificate's Subject CN and requires a matching cloudPC object (virtualEndpoint/cloudPCs, managedDeviceId eq CN) in the tenant. Only service-provisioned Cloud PCs have such an object, so no other enrolled device can pass this stage. Requires the optional Graph permission CloudPC.Read.All (feature "W365CloudPcValidation" in the grant script).

fields.name: validateIntuneDeviceBinding
fields.doc: Cert-to-device binding check (Global-Admin-only preview, SHADOW mode). Resolves the Intune managedDevice id carried in the agent client certificate's Subject CN against this tenant's own managedDevices inventory, proving the certificate belongs to a device the tenant actually enrolled. The result is recorded as telemetry only and never blocks enrollment, because a device object can in principle appear later than the agent's first call - measuring that race is the point of the shadow pass. Requires the optional Graph permission DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All (feature "IntuneDeviceBinding" in the grant script).

fields.name: allowInsecureAgentRequests
fields.doc: Emergency bypass for agent security gate (Global Admin use only). If true, agent requests are accepted even when ValidateAutopilotDevice is false. Default: false

fields.name: dataRetentionDays
fields.doc: Data retention period in days Sessions and events older than this will be deleted by the daily maintenance job Default: 90 days

fields.name: sessionTimeoutHours
fields.doc: Session inactivity timeout in hours. Once an "InProgress" session is idle past this, the maintenance sweep reclassifies it out of "InProgress" (see tasks/enrollment-status-reclassification.md): if Device Setup already finished it becomes AwaitingUser (non-terminal), otherwise it eventually settles as the terminal, non-failure Incomplete state once SessionGraceHours elapses — it is NOT counted as a failure. This prevents stalled sessions from running indefinitely and skewing statistics. Recommended: Use the same value as your ESP (Enrollment Status Page) timeout Default: 5 hours

fields.name: sessionGraceHours
fields.doc: Grace window in hours for a session that reached the inactivity timeout with Device Setup already provisioned but no completion signal yet (tasks/enrollment-status-reclassification.md). At SessionTimeoutHours such a session becomes AwaitingUser (non-terminal) instead of Failed; only after this window elapses without a completion does it graduate to the terminal, non-failure Incomplete state. 0 (default) = auto-derive: AbsoluteMaxSessionHours + buffer (= 48h + 3h = 51h with defaults). The grace is always floored at the agent's absolute session-age cap plus buffer — until that cap fires the agent may still be legitimately enrolling, and because the cap is silent to the backend anything still quiet past cap+buffer is provably dead. A non-zero value acts as an override but can only raise the effective grace above that floor, never below it (see EnrollmentTimeoutClassifier.ResolveGraceHours).

fields.name: maxNdjsonPayloadSizeMB
fields.doc: Maximum decompressed ingest-batch payload size in MB, enforced on the JSON-array ingest path (/api/agent/telemetry) — DoS/memory-exhaustion protection. The property name is historical (from the removed V1 NDJSON path); scope is shape-agnostic. Default: 5 MB. Table-only setting (not editable via the tenant-config public API).

fields.name: enablePerformanceCollector
fields.doc: Enable Performance Collector (CPU, memory, disk, network monitoring) Generates ~1 event per interval - can create significant traffic Default: true

fields.name: performanceCollectorIntervalSeconds
fields.doc: Performance collector interval in seconds Default: 30 seconds

fields.name: helloWaitTimeoutSeconds
fields.doc: Seconds to wait for the Windows Hello wizard after ESP exit Default: 30 seconds

fields.name: maxAuthFailures
fields.doc: Maximum consecutive authentication failures (401/403) before the agent shuts down. null = use default (5). 0 = disabled (retry forever).

fields.name: authFailureTimeoutMinutes
fields.doc: Maximum time in minutes the agent keeps retrying after the first auth failure. null = use default (0 = disabled, only MaxAuthFailures applies).

fields.name: agentMaxLifetimeMinutes
fields.doc: Maximum agent lifetime in minutes. Safety net to prevent zombie agents. null = use default (360 = 6 hours). 0 = disabled (no lifetime limit).

fields.name: absoluteMaxSessionHours
fields.doc: Absolute per-session age cap in hours enforced by the agent's emergency break (Program.Guards.CheckSessionAgeEmergencyBreak → AgentConfiguration.AbsoluteMaxSessionHours). null = agent default (48). Mirrored here so the backend can derive the session-grace floor from the same value: the timeout grace is never shorter than this cap + buffer. NOTE: the agent still reads its own AbsoluteMaxSessionHours today; wiring this override down to the agent config response is a follow-up so the two stay in lockstep.

fields.name: selfDestructOnComplete
fields.doc: Whether to self-destruct after enrollment completion (remove Scheduled Task and all files). null = use agent default (true).

fields.name: keepLogFile
fields.doc: Preserve logs during self-destruct. null = use agent default (false).

fields.name: rebootOnComplete
fields.doc: Whether to reboot the device after enrollment completes. null = use agent default (false).

fields.name: rebootDelaySeconds
fields.doc: Delay in seconds before the reboot is initiated (shutdown.exe /r /t X). null = use agent default (10 seconds).

fields.name: enableGeoLocation
fields.doc: Whether to enable geo-location detection (queries external IP service). null = use agent default (true).

fields.name: ntpServer
fields.doc: NTP server address for time check during enrollment. null = use agent default ("time.windows.com").

fields.name: enableTimezoneAutoSet
fields.doc: Whether to automatically set the device timezone based on IP geolocation. Requires EnableGeoLocation to be true. Uses tzutil /s to apply. null = use agent default (false).

fields.name: enableDoGroupIdAutoSet
fields.doc: Whether to set the Delivery Optimization group ID (DOGroupId policy value) from a network fingerprint: a deterministic GUID derived from the default gateway's IP and MAC address, so devices on the same local network peer with each other (byte layout is RealmJoin-compatible). Only takes effect with DO Download Mode = Group (2); existing DOGroupId/DOGroupIdSource policies (Intune/GPO) are never overwritten. null = use agent default (false).

fields.name: enableImeMatchLog
fields.doc: Whether to write a match log for every IME log line matched by a pattern. When true, the agent writes to the default path Constants.ImeMatchLogPath. null = use agent default (false).

fields.name: enableGatherRuleDebugLog
fields.doc: Whether the agent writes a local gather-rule evaluation trace file so customers can diagnose rules that produce no timeline events (scope skips, on_change suppression, empty collector results, logparser details). When true, the agent writes to Constants.GatherRuleDebugLogPath. The trace never leaves the device. null = use agent default (false).

fields.name: enableEspContinueAnywayObservation
fields.doc: Continue-Anyway observation mode: when true AND the ESP profile allows "Continue anyway", a Device-phase ESP terminal failure (AccountSetup never entered) does not fail the session immediately — the agent keeps monitoring for up to 60 minutes and completes with an esp-soft-failure marker once the DAD-validated real-user desktop (plus the Hello gate) proves the user continued; an expired window fails with the original esp_terminal_failure. Operator-set only (not exposed in the tenant admin UI). null = use agent default (false).

fields.name: logLevel
fields.doc: Log verbosity level override for this tenant's agents. null = use agent default ("Info"). Values: "Info", "Debug", "Verbose", "Trace".

fields.name: maxBatchSize
fields.doc: Maximum events per upload batch. null = use agent default (100).

fields.name: showEnrollmentSummary
fields.doc: Whether to show a visual enrollment summary dialog to the end user after enrollment completes (success or failure). null = use agent default (false).

fields.name: enrollmentSummaryTimeoutSeconds
fields.doc: Auto-close timeout in seconds for the enrollment summary dialog. null = use agent default (60). 0 = no auto-close.

fields.name: enrollmentSummaryBrandingImageUrl
fields.doc: Optional URL to a branding image displayed as a banner at the top of the enrollment summary dialog. Expected size: 540 x 80 px. Larger images will be center-cropped.

fields.name: enrollmentSummaryLaunchRetrySeconds
fields.doc: Maximum time in seconds the agent retries launching the enrollment summary dialog when the user's desktop is locked by a credential UI (e.g. Windows Hello). null = use agent default (120). 0 = no retry (single attempt).

fields.name: showScriptOutput
fields.doc: Whether to show PowerShell script stdout in the web UI. When false, only stderr (error output) is visible for troubleshooting. stdout may contain sensitive data (credentials, tokens). Default true (show stdout). Data is always collected regardless of this setting.

fields.name: enableLocalAdminAnalyzer
fields.doc: Whether the LocalAdminAnalyzer is enabled for this tenant's devices. null = use agent default (true).

fields.name: enableSoftwareInventoryAnalyzer
fields.doc: Whether the SoftwareInventoryAnalyzer is enabled for this tenant's devices. null = use agent default (true).

fields.name: enableIntegrityBypassAnalyzer
fields.doc: Whether the IntegrityBypassAnalyzer is enabled for this tenant's devices. null = use agent default (true).

fields.name: enableRealmJoinWatcher
fields.doc: Whether the RealmJoin watcher is enabled for this tenant's devices. RealmJoin enrollment-package tracking is off by default; enable only for tenants that deploy via RealmJoin. null = use agent default (false).

fields.name: keepAwakeDuringUserEsp
fields.doc: Whether to keep the device awake during the User-ESP (AccountSetup) phase for this tenant's devices. Prevents idle standby/sleep from stalling app installs / account provisioning; reboots are unaffected. Off by default. null = use agent default (false).

fields.name: enableConsoleBypassDetection
fields.doc: Whether to detect a SYSTEM console opened during enrollment (Shift+F10 OOBE bypass) for this tenant's devices. Gates the live ConsoleBypass watcher + the startup prefetch scanner. On by default (opt-out); tenants that knowingly use Shift+F10 for support can disable it. null = use agent default (true).

fields.name: localAdminAllowedAccountsJson
fields.doc: JSON-serialized list of additional local account names that are considered expected on a newly enrolled device (merged with built-in defaults on the agent). Example: ["SupportAdmin", "TechDesk"]

fields.name: bootstrapTokenEnabled
fields.doc: Per-tenant ADDITIVE enable for OOBE Bootstrap Sessions (Global Admin only). The Pro plan includes the feature regardless of this flag; for Community tenants this is the on-request escape hatch. Effective value = plan-included OR this flag — resolved via TenantEntitlementService.IsBootstrapEnabled (backend); when effectively false, the feature is hidden in the UI and all bootstrap API endpoints reject requests.

fields.name: unrestrictedModeEnabled
fields.doc: Whether the Unrestricted Mode feature is available for this tenant (the Pro-plan on-request gate). When false (default), the Unrestricted Mode section is hidden in the tenant settings UI and UnrestrictedMode cannot be activated by tenant admins. Only configurable by Global Admins.

fields.name: unrestrictedMode
fields.doc: When effective, agent guardrails are relaxed: all registry paths, WMI queries, and commands are allowed via GatherRules. File paths and diagnostics paths are allowed except C:\Users. Default: false. Can only be toggled by tenant admins when UnrestrictedModeEnabled is true. EFFECTIVE only while the tenant's edition is Pro (read-time re-gate, fail-closed on trial expiry/downgrade) — see TenantEntitlementService.IsUnrestrictedModeActive.

fields.name: entraAppRolesEnabled
fields.doc: When enabled, tenant member roles (Admin / Operator) may also be granted via Entra ID app-role assignments on the application's Enterprise App (the "roles" claim in the user's token), in addition to the TenantAdmins table. Resolution is table-first: an explicit TenantAdmins entry always overrides a claim-derived role (e.g. to grant an Operator CanManageBootstrapTokens). Only Admin and Operator are claim-mappable; the platform-wide GlobalAdmin role is never derived from claims. Off by default — per-tenant opt-in. Backend-only setting: not delivered to the agent (no ConfigVersion impact).

fields.name: diagnosticsLogPathsJson
fields.doc: JSON-serialized list of tenant-specific additional log paths/wildcards to include in the diagnostics ZIP package (additive to global paths). Each entry: { "path": "...", "description": "...", "isBuiltIn": false }

fields.name: diagnosticsBlobSasUrl
fields.doc: Azure Blob Storage Container SAS URL for diagnostics package upload. Used only when DiagnosticsUploadDestination is "CustomerSas". Each tenant provides their own container — data stays in the customer's storage. If null or empty (and destination is CustomerSas), diagnostics upload is disabled.

fields.name: diagnosticsUploadMode
fields.doc: When to upload diagnostics packages: "Off", "Always", "OnFailure". Applies to both destinations. Default: "Off"

fields.name: diagnosticsUploadDestination
fields.doc: Where diagnostics packages should be uploaded: "CustomerSas" (default) — customer's own storage account via the SAS URL in . Preserves existing behaviour; no data leaves the customer's Azure tenant boundary."Hosted" — opt-in only. Blobs land in the backend's storage account under {tenantId}/AgentDiagnostics-...zip in the container. Requires an explicit admin click in the tenant settings UI with a clearly-marked "data leaves your tenant" disclosure — never set silently. Default "CustomerSas" so existing tenants without the field set behave identically to today and customer data is never silently routed to hosted storage.

fields.name: sendTraceEvents
fields.doc: Whether the agent should send Trace-severity events to the backend. Trace events capture key agent decisions for backend-side troubleshooting. Default: true (on in preview). Can be disabled per tenant to reduce traffic.

fields.name: teamsWebhookUrl
fields.doc: URL of the Teams Incoming Webhook for enrollment notifications. If null or empty, no notifications are sent.

fields.name: teamsNotifyOnSuccess
fields.doc: Send a Teams notification when an enrollment completes successfully. Default: true

fields.name: teamsNotifyOnFailure
fields.doc: Send a Teams notification when an enrollment fails. Default: true

fields.name: teamsNotifyOnStart
fields.doc: Send a Teams notification when an enrollment starts (session registration). Opt-in: default false to avoid surprising existing tenants with a notification storm.

fields.name: webhookProviderType
fields.doc: Webhook provider type. Determines which renderer formats the notification payload. 0=None, 1=TeamsLegacyConnector, 2=TeamsWorkflowWebhook, 10=Slack. Legacy tenants with TeamsWebhookUrl are auto-resolved via GetEffectiveWebhookConfig().

fields.name: webhookUrl
fields.doc: Generic webhook URL for enrollment notifications. Replaces TeamsWebhookUrl for new configurations.

fields.name: webhookNotifyOnSuccess
fields.doc: Send a webhook notification when enrollment succeeds. Default: true.

fields.name: webhookNotifyOnFailure
fields.doc: Send a webhook notification when enrollment fails. Default: true.

fields.name: webhookNotifyOnHardwareRejection
fields.doc: Send a webhook notification when a device is rejected by the hardware whitelist. Default: false (opt-in).

fields.name: webhookNotifyOnStart
fields.doc: Send a webhook notification when an enrollment starts (session registration on the backend). Opt-in: default false to avoid surprising existing tenants with a notification storm.

fields.name: webhookCustomHeadersJson
fields.doc: Custom HTTP request headers (JSON object: { "Header-Name": "value", ... }) sent with every generic-webhook POST. Used for API-key authentication against ticketing systems / SMTP gateways. Only applied when the effective provider is GenericJson. Restricted headers (Host, Content-Length, Content-Type, etc.) are ignored — see GetGenericWebhookHeaders.

fields.name: notificationChannelsJson
fields.doc: Named notification channels as a JSON array (camelCase, see NotificationChannel). Supersedes the single WebhookUrl/WebhookProviderType pair: each channel carries its own provider, URL, custom headers and per-event opt-in toggles, and analyze rules can target specific channels by id. Null/empty = tenant not migrated yet — GetNotificationChannels then synthesizes one channel from the legacy fields so existing tenants keep their exact behavior without a data migration.

fields.name: slaTargetSuccessRate
fields.doc: Target enrollment success rate as a percentage (e.g. 95.0 = 95%). null = SLA tracking disabled for this tenant.

fields.name: slaTargetMaxDurationMinutes
fields.doc: Target maximum enrollment duration in minutes (P95 threshold). Sessions exceeding this are considered SLA violators.

fields.name: slaTargetAppInstallSuccessRate
fields.doc: Target app install success rate as a percentage (e.g. 98.0 = 98%). Only evaluated when enough installs exist (20+).

fields.name: slaNotifyOnSuccessRateBreach
fields.doc: Send notification when enrollment success rate drops below threshold.

fields.name: slaSuccessRateNotifyThreshold
fields.doc: Warning threshold for success rate notifications. Defaults to SlaTargetSuccessRate when null. Allows a separate warning level (e.g. target 99%, notify at 95%).

fields.name: slaNotifyOnDurationBreach
fields.doc: Send notification when P95 enrollment duration exceeds SlaTargetMaxDurationMinutes.

fields.name: slaNotifyOnAppInstallBreach
fields.doc: Send notification when app install success rate drops below SlaTargetAppInstallSuccessRate.

fields.name: slaNotifyOnConsecutiveFailures
fields.doc: Send notification when consecutive enrollment failures reach the threshold.

fields.name: slaConsecutiveFailureThreshold
fields.doc: Number of consecutive enrollment failures that triggers a notification. Default: 5.

Adding a field here is a deliberate decision that the field is non-sensitive (no webhook URLs, SAS tokens, allowlists, addresses).

fields.name: bootstrapTokenEnabled

fields.name: diagnosticsUploadConfigured
fields.doc: Whether an on-demand diagnostics upload can succeed right now (mode not Off + usable destination). Deliberately no destination detail.

fields.name: validateAutopilotDevice
fields.doc: Drives the "Autopilot Device Validation disabled" dashboard banner.

fields.name: appHomingFunnelActive
fields.doc: Dual app-reg self-service migration: consent flow targets the NEW app registration. Non-sensitive — exposes no client ids.

fields.name: unrestrictedMode

fields.name: edition
fields.doc: Resolved edition, lowercase ("community" / "pro").

fields.name: editionSource
fields.doc: Why: "community" | "plan" (own Pro tier) | "trial" | "msp" (Pro conferred by the managing tenant — shown as "Pro (MSP)").

fields.name: trialExpiresUtc
fields.doc: Absent unless the tenant is on an active trial.

fields.name: contactEmailSet
fields.doc: Whether a contact address is stored (boolean only — the address stays admin-gated).

fields.name: companyNameSet
fields.doc: Whether a company name is stored (boolean only — the value stays admin-gated).

TenantGroup.doc: A Tenant Group: an app-internal named bundle of tenants. A delegated admin assigned to the group (see TenantGroupAssignment) gains read scope to every tenant in TenantIds. Adding a tenant to the group grants it to all assignees at once.

fields.name: tenantIds
fields.doc: Tenant IDs (lowercase) in this group.

fields.name: assigneeCount
fields.doc: Number of UPNs assigned to this group (== Assignees.Count).

fields.name: assignees
fields.doc: The UPNs assigned to this group (for the management UI).

fields.name: chargeHomeTenantQuota
fields.doc: Operator flag: MCP reads an assignee makes INTO this group's tenants are charged to the assignee's HOME tenant's quota instead of the managed tenant's. For operator-run managed-service groups whose customers must never pay (or be blocked) for the operator's own analysis. Off by default.

fields.name: ownerTenantId
fields.doc: The managing tenant that owns this self-service group (msp-{tenantId}); null for operator-created groups.

TenantGroupAssignment.doc: One UPN→group assignment. PK=UPN, RK=groupId in storage.

fields.name: role
fields.doc: Constants.DelegatedRoles: "DelegatedReader" (default) or "DelegatedAdmin".

TenantGroupListResponse.doc: Response of GET global/tenant-groups: every group with tenants + assignees.

TenantManagerAssignee.doc: One person with access, nested in TenantManagerItem.

TenantManagerItem.doc: One party that can read the caller's tenant, nested in TenantManagerListResponse.

fields.name: groupId
fields.doc: The Tenant Group conferring the access; absent for direct operator grants.

fields.name: ownerTenantId
fields.doc: The managing tenant that owns the group (self-service); absent for operator-created groups and direct grants.

fields.name: source
fields.doc: self-service | operator

fields.name: revocable
fields.doc: True when the caller (the managed tenant's admin) may end this access here.

TenantManagerListResponse.doc: Response of GET delegations/managers: who manages the caller's tenant.

TenantOffboardingCustomsArchiveEntry.doc: Snapshot of a tenant's custom rule row written by the offboarding handler during Phase 2.D-archive, BEFORE the original row is safe-wiped. Survives forever so a Global Admin can review (and selectively delete) the tenant's custom rules from /admin/customs-archive after offboarding completes. Storage layout (see PR3.B plan §3.2): PartitionKey: "{normalizedTenantId}_{historyRowKey}". One partition per offboarding run — Re-Re-Offboarding produces a fresh, immutable partition each time so multiple runs co-exist without RowKey collisions.RowKey: "{originalTable}_{base64url(originalRowKey)}". The table-name prefix disambiguates collisions across the three rules tables; the base64url encoding of avoids the Azure-Tables RowKey-forbidden characters (#, ?, /, \, control chars).

fields.name: partitionKey
fields.doc: "{normalizedTenantId}_{historyRowKey}".

fields.name: rowKey
fields.doc: "{originalTable}_{base64url(originalRowKey)}".

fields.name: originalTable
fields.doc: One of GatherRules / AnalyzeRules / ImeLogPatterns.

fields.name: originalRowKey
fields.doc: Original RowKey verbatim — base64url-encoded into RowKey's suffix.

fields.name: entityJson
fields.doc: JSON dump of every property on the source row (excluding system properties). The full body is small enough to fit in a single Azure Table string property (64 KB limit; observed rule bodies are well under 4 KB). If a future rule type ever exceeds that, an EntityJsonBlobUrl overflow pointer can be added — not part of this PR.

fields.name: historyRowKey
fields.doc: Cross-reference to the OffboardingHistory row for the run.

fields.name: archivedBy
fields.doc: Constant "TenantOffboardingHandler" in production. Test fakes may override.

TestLogPatternResponse.doc: Response of POST rules/gather/test-pattern: the per-line evaluation of a logparser regex with the agent's exact matching semantics.

fields.name: format
fields.doc: "cmtrace" or "text" — the effective mode the lines were evaluated in.

TestNotificationChannelRequest.doc: Body of POST config/{tenantId}/test-notification and POST global/config/test-ops-channel.

TestWebhookNotificationResponse.doc: Response of POST config/{tenantId}/test-notification AND POST global/config/test-ops-channel: the delivery verdict of a test send (HTTP 200 for both verdicts — Success carries the outcome). One shape for both because the semantics are identical; the platform endpoint only differs in which channel list it resolves the id against.

fields.name: statusCode
fields.doc: HTTP status returned by the webhook endpoint, or null when the send never got a response — the key is omitted when null.

TimeAttributionBlockingAppStat.doc: Per-app rollup of ESP-blocking install intervals across the clean sessions of an aggregate row. The what-if numbers are the per-session critical-path savings from removing this app (recomputed union end without it) — an upper BOUND by construction: UI copy must say "up to", never "you will save" (truthfulness rule 3).

fields.name: sessionCount
fields.doc: Clean sessions with a measured interval for this app (row gate: ≥5).

TimeAttributionDailyAggregate.doc: Daily fleet rollup of session time attribution for one (tenant, enrollment class, date) — F1 PR2 (insights spec §F1 "Data & compute changes"). Enrollment classes are never mixed (a WhiteGlove flow has a structurally different time profile than user-driven). Only breakdowns with None enter the statistics; flagged sessions are excluded WITH a disclosed count (truthfulness rule 7). Rows are written even below the ≥20-session UI gate — the UI needs the n to say "insufficient data (n=3)" instead of silently rendering a small-n median (rule 4). Recomputed idempotently by the rolling 30-day maintenance sweep.

fields.name: date
fields.doc: Calendar day (UTC) the sessions STARTED, "yyyy-MM-dd" — same bucketing as the usage snapshots.

fields.name: tenantId
fields.doc: Tenant GUID, or "global" for the cross-tenant row.

fields.name: enrollmentClass
fields.doc: Enrollment class: "user_driven", "whiteglove", "self_deploying" or "device_preparation" (WDP v2).

fields.name: attributionVersion
fields.doc: Attribution algorithm version the underlying breakdowns were computed with (rule 8: never mix definitions).

fields.name: cleanSessionCount
fields.doc: Breakdowns with QualityFlags == None that formed the statistics.

fields.name: flaggedExcludedCount
fields.doc: Flagged breakdowns excluded from the statistics (disclosed, never silent).

fields.name: missingBreakdownCount
fields.doc: Terminal sessions of this bucket without a computable breakdown (e.g. events aged out before backfill).

fields.name: topBlockingApps
fields.doc: Top blocking apps by median interval, gated at ≥5 sessions per app, capped at 20.

TimeAttributionFlags.doc: Data-quality flags for a SessionTimeBreakdown (truthfulness rule 7: problems flag the record and exclude it from fleet aggregates with a disclosed count, rather than silently skewing them).

TimeAttributionMetricsResponse.doc: Response of GET metrics/time-attribution and GET global/metrics/time-attribution: the rolling 30-day range statistics per enrollment class plus the daily rows for the per-day trend. The range window is FIXED at the sweep's 30 days.

fields.name: classes
fields.doc: Range statistics per enrollment class (never mixed), class-name ordinal order.

fields.name: daily
fields.doc: Daily rows of the window, date ordinal order.

TimeAttributionSegmentStat.doc: Distribution of one attribution segment across the clean sessions of an aggregate row. Values are whole seconds; a session that has no span of this segment contributes 0 — the distribution answers "time spent in this segment per enrollment of this class", not "per enrollment that happened to enter it".

fields.name: segmentKey
fields.doc: Segment key (TimeAttributionSegments), including "unattributed" — the stack must sum to the wall clock (truthfulness rule 2).

TimeAttributionSpan.doc: One contiguous attributed span inside an observation window.

fields.name: segmentKey
fields.doc: Segment key — one of the TimeAttributionSegments constants (never "unattributed": the remainder is a scalar, not a span claim).

fields.name: seconds
fields.doc: Whole seconds (floored). The sub-second dust lands in the unattributed remainder — never invented into a segment.

TopCve.doc: A single CVE ranked by how many devices it affects in scope. EpssScore is the highest EPSS probability seen across the rows (null = unscored / legacy rows); Priority the highest act/attend/track band (empty on legacy rows).

TopFailingApp.doc: An app with a high failure rate.

TpmPssUnsupportedItem.doc: One serial-number bucket in the GetTpmPssUnsupported aggregation. All values are self-reported by devices through the unauthenticated distress channel — UNVERIFIED.

TpmPssUnsupportedResponse.doc: Success body of GET audit/tpm-pss-unsupported: devices whose TPM cannot perform RSA-PSS signing, aggregated by serial number over the distress-report retention window.

fields.name: totalRawReports
fields.doc: Count of raw TpmPssUnsupported distress reports before aggregation.

fields.name: epssError

fields.name: syncedAt

fields.name: msrcError
fields.doc: Error text of a failed run; null (key omitted) on success.

fields.name: syncedAt
fields.doc: Preformatted ISO-8601 timestamp of this response.

TriggerNvdCacheRefreshResponse.doc: Response of POST vulnerability/sync-nvd (202): the background walk was started.

fields.name: startedAt
fields.doc: Preformatted ISO-8601 start timestamp.

TriggerVulnerabilityDataSyncResponse.doc: Response of POST vulnerability/sync: KEV refresh plus optional CPE reseed counts.

fields.name: cpeSeedError
fields.doc: Error text of a failed seed reseed; null (key omitted) when skipped or successful.

fields.name: cpeCommunityError
fields.doc: Error text of a failed community reseed; null (key omitted) when skipped or successful.

fields.name: syncedAt
fields.doc: Preformatted ISO-8601 timestamp of this response.

UnmatchedSoftwareItem.doc: One unmatched software title (no CPE mapping), aggregated across tenants. Mutable on purpose: the aggregation sums Frequency and keeps the most recent sighting.

fields.name: frequency
fields.doc: Sum of SessionCount across all tenants' rows for this title.

UpdateSessionReportNoteRequest.doc: Body of PATCH global/session-reports/{reportId}/note; empty clears the note.

fields.name: homedApp
fields.doc: "primary" or "legacy" — the app the tenant resolves to after the call.

fields.name: homedAppClientId
fields.doc: Explicit homing pin, or null (legacy default) — the key is omitted when null.

fields.name: lastAuthClientId

UpdateTenantConfigurationResponse.doc: Response of PUT config/{tenantId}: acknowledgement plus the stored tenant configuration.

UpdateTenantGroupRequest.doc: Body of PATCH global/tenant-groups/{groupId} — at least one field.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: New display name; omitted/blank = unchanged.

fields.name: chargeHomeTenantQuota
fields.doc: See ChargeHomeTenantQuota; omitted = unchanged.

UpsertSessionAnnotationDeletedResponse.doc: Response of PUT sessions/{sessionId}/annotations/{lane} when both verdict and note were empty and the lane was cleared.

UpsertSessionAnnotationRequest.doc: Body of PUT sessions/{sessionId}/annotations/{lane}; both fields empty = clear the lane.

UpsertSessionAnnotationResponse.doc: Response of PUT sessions/{sessionId}/annotations/{lane} on a successful upsert: the stored annotation as the session-scoped endpoints would return it.

fields.name: total
fields.doc: Total unique users (available after Entra ID integration)

fields.name: dailyLogins
fields.doc: Daily logins across all users

fields.name: active7Days
fields.doc: Active users in last 7 days

fields.name: active30Days
fields.doc: Active users in last 30 days

fields.name: note
fields.doc: Note about availability

UserUsageDailySummary.doc: Aggregated daily usage summary across endpoints (and optionally users).

UserUsageRecord.doc: A single usage record: one user, one day, one endpoint.

ValidatorType.doc: Identifies which validator authorized the device during session registration. Surfaced in the RegisterSession response so the agent can reconcile against its own registry-based detection and, when needed, switch its enrollment flow.

VerdictCalibrationAlert.doc: One ACTIVE verdict-calibration alert episode (operator-only). Persisted as the verdictcalibration|{kind}|{path}|{status} keyspace of the notification tracker — the row IS the dedup (one ops event per episode) and the alerts[] payload of the calibration endpoint. Deleted when the signal re-arms (share back under 1.5× baseline, path stops occurring, evidence-gap share back under 15 %) or by the tracker's 30-day retention sweep. Numbers refresh on every radar pass; FirstNotifiedAt never moves. Dimension concentration is CORRELATION only — every consumer says so.

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: One of VerdictCalibrationAlertKinds.

fields.name: verdictPath
fields.doc: Verdict path, or the group label for group kinds ("sweep+maxlife", "r6").

fields.name: status
fields.doc: Status the path produced, or "*" for group kinds.

fields.name: lift
fields.doc: Window rate ÷ baseline rate. Null when the baseline rate is 0 or the kind is absolute (evidence gap).

fields.name: dimension
fields.doc: Dimension concentration captured when the alert FIRST fired; null = no clear concentration.

VerdictCalibrationPathRow.doc: One verdict path × status row of the calibration matrix.

fields.name: reEnrollRatePct
fields.doc: Null below the minimum eligible count — never a rate on a handful of sessions.

fields.name: lift
fields.doc: Window share ÷ baseline share; null when the baseline share is 0 (a new path has no finite lift — never invented).

VerdictCalibrationResponse.doc: Response of GET global/metrics/verdict-calibration: per verdict path, how many sessions it produced in the window, its share, overrides attributed to the prior path, the 7-day re-enrollment proxy, a 7d-vs-28d trend, and the active drift alerts. Operator-only classifier diagnostics.

fields.name: tenantId
fields.doc: Partition echo: a tenant GUID, or "global" for the cross-tenant aggregate.

fields.name: windowStart
fields.doc: Inclusive window start ("yyyy-MM-dd").

fields.name: windowEnd
fields.doc: Inclusive window end ("yyyy-MM-dd", today).

fields.name: computedAt
fields.doc: Newest aggregate compute time in the window; absent when the window holds no rows.

fields.name: versions
fields.doc: Distinct aggregation algorithm versions contributing to the window, ascending.

fields.name: paths
fields.doc: Rows ordered by count descending, then path/status ordinal.

fields.name: alerts
fields.doc: Active drift episodes, newest first.

VerdictCalibrationTotals.doc: Window totals of the calibration matrix.

fields.name: days
fields.doc: Aggregate days that contributed to the window.

VerdictCalibrationTrendMeta.doc: Trend denominators shared by every row (single source, never per-row copies).

VerdictCalibrationTrendWindow.doc: One trend window of a path row.
